confirmed_blocking.evidence: Probe P1e (plain and supabase, identical): claim_first - A runs claim_signup_grant(v) and holds the transaction; B inserts org_members(personal_org(v), w, 'member'): B waited=False, finished while A open, rowcount 1; after A commits: members=2, wallet bound. member_first - A inserts the member and holds; B claims: B waited=False, answers granted; members=2, wallet bound. In both, checks_credit.attempt(credit_job(..., personal_org, wallet)) -> None: admission through the now-shared bound org is accepted, so the second member's keys spend the owner's 10,000 CREDIT. The state is also irreversible under the guard (deletes of the extra member are refused by the same trigger, check_binding 'the owner leaves' case). Cause: the guard reads credit_wallets with a statement snapshot and takes no lock; grant_signup_credit counts members and inserts the wallet with no lock on the organization row; only the FK KEY SHARE is taken, which conflicts with nothing either side holds. Reachable only by the platform role (browser roles cannot write memberships), during the claim transaction's duration; but it is a stated invariant with a sequential-only test, and the consequence is another individual spending the grant.

votes.reason: Confirmed by code reading and by experiment. Code: infrx.personal_org_binding_guard (0015:69-84) does a plain `exists` on infrx.credit_wallets under a READ COMMITTED statement snapshot and takes no lock; infrx.grant_signup_credit (0006:513-522) counts org_members and inserts the wallet without locking the organizations row; claim_signup_grant locks only profiles FOR KEY SHARE. The only locks the two paths share are FK KEY SHARE on organizations/profiles, which do not conflict with each other. No other trigger or lock on org_members, organizations or credit_wallets exists in 0001-0015 (grepped). Experiment (scratch script at /tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/p1e.py, pointing tests/d/pgharness at my own container infrx-review-a1r2-verify-0-0:55534 on the pinned plain image, migrations applied via infrx.state.migrations.sql_for, fixtures via checks.seed_fixtures + checks_credit.seed_credit, race via the suite's own checks_signup._behind; container removed after): claim_first -> B's org_members insert did not wait (no 'waited'), rowcount 1; after A commits: members=2, wallet bound=1; checks_credit.attempt(credit_job(personal_org(v), wallet_of(v))) returned None (admission through the now-shared bound org accepted); deleting the extra member refused with 23514 'membership ... is frozen' (irreversible). member_first -> B's claim did not wait and answered 'granted'; members=2, wallet bound=1. The mechanism (snapshot read + no conflicting lock) is image-independent, so the reviewer's supabase-image result is credible without a second run. Severity: it violates the unconditional invariant stated in the 0015 header and 02, with a money consequence (a second member's keys spend the owner's 10,000 CREDIT) and an unrecoverable state under the guard; the window is narrow (platform role only, during the claim transaction) and the proposed fix is two lock lines in 0015, so it is cheap to close before merge.

CONFIRMED by code and by experiment on my own container (infrx-review-a1r2-verify-0-1, port 55535, plain image, removed afterwards; script at /tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/race.py using the A1 harness at head d8a3e84). Code: `infrx.personal_org_binding_guard` (0015:69-84) only does `exists (select 1 from infrx.credit_wallets ...)` with no lock, so an uncommitted wallet row is invisible to it; `grant_signup_credit` (0006:513-522) counts org_members and inserts the wallet without locking the organization row; the only locks either side takes are FK KEY SHARE on organizations/profiles, which do not conflict with each other. Measured (both orders): claim_first: A `claim_signup_grant(v)` -> granted, held open; B `insert org_members(personal_org(v), w, 'member')` rowcount 1, waited 0.004s, not blocked while A was open; after A commits: members=2, wallet bound to the org. member_first: A holds the member insert; B's claim answers `granted` in 0.014s, unblocked; members=2, wallet bound. In both: `checks_credit.attempt(credit_job(..., org, wallet))` -> None (admission through the now two-member bound org accepted), and `delete` of the extra member -> 23514 'membership ... is frozen' (state irreversible under the guard). This is a new defect, distinct from round-1 items; the header lines 18-19 and the guard comment ("this holds for the platform role too") state the invariant this violates. Caveat on reach: no product code path in apps/ writes org_members (grep finds only tests; 0001's signup trigger inserts the owner only), so exploitation needs a service-role membership write inside the claim transaction's window. Severity kept as blocking because the invariant is explicitly claimed for the platform role, the resulting state cannot be repaired through the guard, and the fix is two lock lines in 0015.

nonblocking.claim_broken: R-A1 says retirement 'renames each personal org the user alone owns'. The loop's actual scope is every organization the user CREATED and alone owns, and its created_by boundary has no killable test: a solo side org (created + owned, no wallet) is renamed 'retired' and suspended (P1b: ('retired', True)); an org the user solely owns but did not create is left alive with a retired sole owner (P1c: ('d', False)); a team whose only two members are both retired (concurrently or sequentially) stays alive with 2 retired members (P1d).
